newsitem.title: CANADA: CITIES BATTLE FOR 2004 OLYMPIC GAMES.
newsitem.headline: CITIES BATTLE FOR 2004 OLYMPIC GAMES.

text.p: The five cities bidding to host the Summer Olympics in 2004 have been using one of their last chances to present their cases this week.

The Pan American Sports Organisation's General Assembly runnning through Sunday is the final opportunity for presentations to International Olympic Committee members prior to final bids in September in Lausanne, Switzerland, where the IOC will make its selection.
Athens, Greece; Buenos Aires, Argentina; Cape Town, South Africa; Rome, Italy; and Stockholm, Sweden, are all in the race.

But two cities -- Cape Town and Buenos Aires -- represent continents which have never hosted the Olympic Games. They are asking the IOC members when the Olympics will be held in Africa or South America.

"Nobody among the five cities is being touted as a clear winner," Carol Anne Letheren, chief executive officer of the Canadian Olympic Association, said at the Pan American Sports Organisation (PASO) annual meeting.
"They all have a unique theme. Buenos Aires has bid five times and the Olympics have never been there.
"It has never been on the African continent and it would be a celebration of the collapse of apartheid.

"The bid cities must convince the IOC members they can technically put on the event, that they have the human resources and the financial resources and those other issues will become added value," she said.

The bid from Athens calls for events to be held in locations of major Olympic significance such as the town of Marathon. The Olympic marathon event would start there and end in the stadium in Athens where the Olympic Games were revived in the year 1896.

At the PASO meetings, 300 delegates from 42 nations also reviewed bids from four cities wanting to host the 2003 Pan American Games. Guadalajara, Mexico; Santiago, Chile; Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic; and Medellin, Columbia, are bidding to host the Games.

Delegate reaction during the presentations gives Guadalajara status as a favourite followed by Santo Domingo, the city which came second to Winnipeg, Canada, for the site of the 1999 Pan Am Games. The final selection for 2003 will take place in 1998 at PASO's General Assembly.
In June 1997 the U.S. Olympic Committee Board of Directors voted to support a U.S. city interested in bidding for the 2007 Pan Am Games rather than to support a 2008 Olympic Summer Games bid.
Four cities -- Dade County (Miami), Florida; Houston, Texas; Raleigh, North Carolina; and San Antonio, Texas -- have expressed their intent to bid for those Pan Am Games.

PASO is also asking the International Olympic Committee to designate the Pan Am Games as the qualifier for all Pan Am nations for the Summer Olympics to ensure the top athletes from all countries compete at the Pan Am Games.

The U.S. Olympic Committee and the Canadian Olympic Committee will send their top athletes and as many as 12 international federations will use the Pan Am Games in Winnipeg two years from now as qualifiers for the Olympic Summer Games in Sydney in 2000.
